I am deliberately not verifying memory_73; its consolidated form already carries its own counter-evidence and an explicit 'do not repeat at scale' verdict, so it is the memory I least need to re-read. The competitor's entry pricing creates obvious pull toward promotional_pricing, and that is precisely the trap memory_73 documents: trial starts +31% and quarterly revenue +18% looked like a win, while churn at renewal rose 12 points. Against a stated objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, matching a discount would convert a competitive squeeze into a book of accounts that leave, so I am declining it even though it is the most direct response to the competitive event. Downstream value risk is real for my chosen action too, and I am flagging it rather than assuming it away. Stripping signup fields and shortening onboarding can raise completion by admitting and rushing accounts that were never qualified, and memory_44 warns that enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows, so an over-simplified self-serve path could quietly divert enterprise traffic out of the demo-request route and degrade pipeline quality while the headline completion number improves. Guardrails: restrict the simplification to the self-serve/SMB path and leave enterprise routing and the demo-request CTA untouched; keep a holdout; and pre-register renewal-cohort retention and qualified-pipeline quality as decision metrics alongside completion, so this experiment cannot be declared a success on the same short-horizon evidence that made the discount campaign look good.
